capabilities: Classify the currently opened note into configured tags
Classify all notes that lack the configured tags
Write tags to frontmatter while leaving existing tags untouched
Configure tag combination policies and per-tag descriptions
Choose between a local Ollama backend and a TypeSafe API backend
extras: The README's 'Similar Projects' section is cut off mid-sentence. It warns that the TypeSafe API key is stored unencrypted in data.json, that classification can overwrite existing auto-generated tags, and recommends backing up files before classifying all notes. Only decision models compatible with Ollama's /v1/systemone endpoint work; ordinary chat models do not. The manifest carries the standard not-manually-reviewed disclaimer.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to assign tags to notes automatically, so tagging large vaults by hand is slow and inconsistent.

relations.evidence: run this classification locally on consumer hardware using ollama
get an API key at TypeSafe and enter it in the settings

summary: Automatic tagger that classifies Markdown notes into configured frontmatter tags using decision models run locally via Ollama or a TypeSafe API.
